clue.text: Store up outrageous riposte

indicators.note: outrageous suggests something wild and out of order, so the letters of the next word are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiles a shocking comeback for later use.
explanation.definitionFit: To reposit is to deposit or lay away for safekeeping, a synonym of storing.

clue.text: Useful for character enlargement?

parts.note: character here means a printed letter, not a personality; the thing described makes small print look bigger to the reader

explanation.walkthrough: 'Character enlargement' suggests building up someone's personality; the characters are letters of type.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles worn for reading magnify the letters on the page.

clue.text: Paint saki possibly as one from Asia

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters given could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Painting a bottle of rice wine marks someone out as Asian.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Pakistan, a country in South Asia, is a person from that continent.

clue.text: Rushed round the north to invest

indicators.note: round means the first word's letters go around the abbreviation

parts.note: rushed means sped

explanation.surface: Someone hurried around the north of the country looking to put money in.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest time or money is to lay it out, the same as spending it.

clue.text: Prepared lousy diet in boring way

indicators.note: prepared hints at food being made up from ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook made a miserable diet plan, and it was dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something dully or wearisomely is doing it in a boring manner.

clue.text: Some students go back for ideal holiday spot

indicators.note: go back tells us the whole run of letters is to be read in the opposite direction

parts.note: some means part
NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK

explanation.surface: A few students head home to find a perfect vacation place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go back' turns PART + NUS into SUNTRAP. The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltered sunny place is where holidaymakers like to bask.

clue.text: Strikes seen in the footwear industry

explanation.surface: Industrial action breaks out among shoemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hits or punches are socks; stockings worn on the feet belong to the footwear trade.

clue.text: Number puzzle? Expression of acquiescence

parts.note: a puzzle is a problem to be solved

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a number puzzle and gets a cheerful agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'it's fine, happy to' is a way of agreeing readily.

clue.text: English in the borders of French city

indicators.note: in places the letter for English inside the word for borders

parts.note: the borders of something are its rims

explanation.surface: An Englishman finds himself on the edge of a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the borders' is not a selection of the outer letters of 'French' but a synonym, RIMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Reims is a city in the Champagne region of north-east France.

clue.text: Ale passed around with another drink. Delighted!

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink, a second one after the ale

explanation.surface: Beer is handed round at a party with a further beverage, to everyone's joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like part of the passing of drinks, but it signals the anagram; 'another drink' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hugely happy, the same as overjoyed.

clue.text: Joint to cause continuous irritation (not right)

indicators.note: not right means the letter R, for right, is dropped

parts.note: to rankle is to cause lasting resentment

explanation.surface: Something in a joint keeps niggling but isn't quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' takes the R out of RANKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint between the foot and the leg is this one.

clue.text: It's misleading to change TV piece (Ed.)

indicators.note: change tells us the following letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An editor is told that altering a television feature makes it false.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gives a false impression is misleading.

clue.text: At home, man with debts is cunning

parts.note: being in means being at home
Sid is a man's name
IOUs are notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: A man stays home owing money, and turns out to be crafty.
explanation.definitionFit: Insidious means sly and treacherous, working stealthily to harm.

clue.text: The fertile spot could be a support for flowers

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether a green patch could hold a flower arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A watered fertile area in a desert; also the trade name of the green foam florists stick stems into.

clue.text: Good bit of money? Great!

explanation.surface: Someone receives a decent sum and is thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'grand' is slang for 1,000 pounds or dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a thousand pounds or dollars; also an exclamation meaning splendid.

clue.text: Reward one on leaving

parts.note: a desert is a deserved reward, as in 'just deserts'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bonus is given to someone as they quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just deserts' means a deserved reward or punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Desertion is abandonment, the act of walking out.

clue.text: SDP bell in unusual entrance

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters are put into an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A political party's bell hangs in an odd doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges SDP BELL IN. The SDP was a British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance, as a verb, is to captivate or enthral.

clue.text: Phoney bits?

parts.note: phoney is read as 'to do with a phone', not as fake, so these are parts of a telephone handset

explanation.walkthrough: 'Phoney' looks like it means fake; it means belonging to a phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone receiver has the parts held to the ear.

clue.text: TV etc, in peculiar item effected without delay

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another
peculiar means odd, so the letters are oddly arranged

parts.note: television and the like make up the media

explanation.surface: A strange television item is made at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram 'peculiar' makes IMTE; 'in' then sets the TV-and-so-on word between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done instantly, with no pause, is immediate.

clue.text: One who contradicts wins? Yes, right

parts.note: wins means gains
aye is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: A winner is told yes, correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny, so such a person disputes what others say.

clue.text: See 1 down
Two graduates capture black snake

indicators.note: capture means the outer piece takes the other inside it
two means the following piece appears twice

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A pair of graduates catch a dark serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' doubles MA; 'capture' puts B inside MAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a venomous African serpent.

clue.text: See 8
Partly eastern flower

indicators.note: partly says only part of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A bloom that is somewhat oriental.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like garden bloom.

clue.text: Some militia raise headwear on formal occasions

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few soldiers lift up hats worn at grand events.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled crown-like band is worn by women at state dinners and weddings.

clue.text: Mixed, as a mob could be?

explanation.surface: A crowd agitated like a stirred drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred describes a mixed liquid; a mob roused to anger has been agitated.

clue.text: Criticised student left, really fed up

indicators.note: left means the student departed, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: slated means harshly criticised
L is the learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student who was criticised walks out, thoroughly fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes L out of SLATED. 'Fed up' here means full of food, not annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sated means fully satisfied with food, stuffed.

clue.text: Locating equipment going up or down

indicators.note: going up or down means the word reads the same in either direction in a down light

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A tracking device that rises and falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar systems find aircraft and ships by bouncing radio waves off them.

clue.text: The piece of numerical data not moving around is "Time"

indicators.note: around means the first word encloses the next pieces

parts.note: static means still

explanation.surface: A still figure turns out to be a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks round "Time" are surface dressing; it simply abbreviates to T, which goes in after IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A single figure from a set of data is a statistic.

clue.text: A cart could be pinched

explanation.surface: A wagon that has been stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cart is horse-pulled; a gaunt, tired face is described as pinched.

clue.text: Society, criticised, went from one side to the other

definitions.text: went from one side to the other

parts.note: panned means harshly criticised

explanation.surface: A club, having been reviewed badly, crossed over.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge that crosses a river is said to bridge it from bank to bank.

clue.text: Rock fragments by church produce a sharp noise

parts.note: scree is loose broken stone on a slope

explanation.surface: Falling stones near a church make a shrill sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To screech is to give a shrill, piercing cry.
